Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.43849 of 2022
Order:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard, Sri Pasham Thrivikram Reddy, learned counsel representing Ms. Ravula Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri Mujeeb Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed challenging the detention order bearing No.44/PD-CELL/CYB/2022,
dated 25.11.2022 of 2nd respondent, confirmed by the 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.81, dated 12.01.2023.
Petitioner, who is friend of the detenue i.e., Mr Goudu Jitendra @ Narsima @Mohan@Varun filed the present Writ Petition.

3. Perusal of record would reveal that two criminal cases were registered against the detenue i.e.,
Cr.No.288 of 2022 pending on the file of Jagathgirigutta Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 370 (A)(2) of IPC and Sections 3,4,5 and 6 of PIT Act and Cr.No.628 of 2022 pending on the file of Kukatpally Police Stattion for the offences punishable under Section 370(A)(2) IPC and Sections 3,4 and 5 of PIT Act.
In both crimes detenue released on 26.05.2022 and 19.09.2022 itself respectively.
In both the bail orders conditions were imposed.

Even then, 2nd respondent has invoked the procedure laid down under Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers,
Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders,
Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders,
Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (For short, 'the Act')

entities.text:
Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers,
Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders,
Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: detained the detenue in Central Prison, Cherlapally, Medchal-Malkarjgir District on 25.11.2022.

The said detention order dated 25.11.2022 was confirmed by 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.81, dated 12.01.2023.
4.

Perusal of record would reveal that though the bail was granted to the detenue in first crime i.e.,
Cr.No.288 of 2022 on 26.05.2022, the respondent authorities have not filed any cancellation of the bail application in the said crime on the ground that detenue herein repeated the very same offences involving in Cr.No.628 of 2022.

It is also relevant to note that though the detenue was released on Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24044968/
1 19.09.2022 in the second crime, the detention order was passed on 25.11.2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondent authorities cannot contend that to prevent the detenue from continuing similar offences immediately they have invoked the procedure laid down under the Act and issued detention order dated 25.11.2022.
5. In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana1 Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere apprehension of breach of law and order cannot be a ground to invoke the harsh provisions of preventive detention.

entities.text: Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The authorities have a remedy to oppose the bail application or file application seeking cancellation of bail, if they feel that release of such person is against the interest of society.
The relevant paragraph is extracted below:

"24. On the facts of this case, as has been pointed out by us, it is clear that at the highest, a possible apprehension of breach of law and order can be said to (2021) 9 SCC 415 be made out if it is apprehended that the Detenu, if set free, will continue to cheat gullible persons.
This may be a good ground to appeal against the bail orders granted and/or to cancel bail but certainly cannot provide the springboard to move under a preventive detention statute.
We, therefore, quash the detention order on this ground.
Consequently, it is unnecessary to go into any of the other grounds argued by the learned Counsel on behalf of the Petitioner.
The impugned judgment is set aside and the Detenu is ordered to be freed forthwith.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed."
6.
Further, preventive detention can only be invoked in respect of habitual offenders.
A person is said to be a habitual offender, if he/she is involved persistently in commission of a crime of the same nature with a degree of continuity.

7. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar2, the Hon'ble Supreme Court explained the phrase 'habitual criminal' as follows:
"12. A person is habitual criminal who by force of-habit or inward disposition,
inherent or latent in him, has grown accustomed to lead a life of crime.

entities.text: Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is the force of habit inherent or latent in an individual with a criminal instinct, (1984) 3 SCC 14.
with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him dangerous to the society in general.

In simple language the word 'habitually' means 'by force of habit'."
8.
In the present case, the Petitioner involved in the commission of two crimes of similar nature.
A person being involved in two crime does not mean that he/she is a habitual criminal.
The burden placed under the law of preventive detention is much higher and the authority has to establish the criminal habits of the proposed detenue.
Merely because two crimes are registered cannot be a reason for detaining a person.

9. In the similar circumstances, this Court vide order dated 29.04.2022 in W.P.No.3844 of 2022,
wherein two crimes were registered against the detenue for the offences punishable under Sections Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24044968/
2 370 (A)(2) IPC and 354 of IPC, set aside the detention order by declaring it as illegal.

entities.text: Sections Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 10. Vide order dated 30.07.2020 in K. Damla vs. the State of Telangana in W.P.No.7132 of 2020, a Division Bench of this Court held that detention order issued after 5 months of the involvement of the detenue therein is illegal.

entities.text: K. Damla vs. the State of Telangana in W.P.No.7132 of 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. As discussed supra, in the present case, respondent authorities have not taken steps of either opposing the bail application or filing application seeking cancellation of the bail.

This Court and Hon'ble Apex Court, time again categorically held that provisions of the Act, 1986 have to be invoked in the rarest of the rare cases in preventing a person from committing the similar offences to prevent the public order but not law and order.
In the present case, respondent authorities failed to do so.

Therefore, the detention order dated 25.11.2022 passed by 2nd respondent confirmed by the 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.81, dated 12.01.2023 are set aside and respondents are directed to set free the detenue i.e., Goudu Jitendra @ Narsimha @Mohan @ Varun S/o Narasimha, aged about 27 years, R/o. flat No.302, Sai Prashanthi Nilayam, Jayanagar, KPHB and N/o H.No.1- 240,
Goudi Veedhi, Liviri Mandlam, Srikakulam District, Andhra Pradesh if he is not required in any other criminal case.
12. Accordingly, this writ petition is allowed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
